primitives.name: Moving Plank Illusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: direction to that in which, a moment previously, we had been seeing the water move, whilst on either side of this band another band of planks will move as the water did.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes constant velocity motion, observer's persistence of visual perception, and local contrast effects.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Illusion fails when motion stops abruptly or when observer fixates on edges.

layer2.mapping: Maps perceptual flow to state-transition dynamics in GSE and belief propagation in GSI.

primitives.name: Car Window Flow
primitives.verbatim_quote: Looking at a waterfall, or at the road from out of a carwindow in a moving train, produces the same illusion, which may be easily verified in the laboratory by a simple piece of apparatus.
primitives.assumptions: Relativistic velocity difference between observer and environment, and neural adaptation to constant motion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Illusion breaks down at high accelerations or sudden changes in scenery.

layer2.mapping: Applies to predicting opponent movement in sports via relative camera-frame analysis in GSE and to updating market expectations based on flow momentum in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Comparing player tracking data against fixed-camera baselines.

primitives.name: Crank Apparatus
primitives.verbatim_quote: A board with a window five or six inches wide and of any convenient length is supported upright on two feet.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rigid body mechanics, frictionless roller systems, and continuous periodic motion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Apparatus fails when friction causes stick-slip behavior or when the crank speed exceeds human perceptual limits.

layer2.mapping: Serves as a foundational physical model for simulating state transitions in GSE and for generating synthetic data in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Measuring angular velocity and jerk to calibrate perceptual models.

primitives.name: Reverse Motion Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: Turning the crank now sets the central band in continuous motion, whilst the margins of the field remain really at rest, but after a while appear moving in the contrary way.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes neural integration time constants and post-stimulus facilitation of opposite motion pathways.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Effect vanishes once the visual system resets to baseline activity levels.

layer2.mapping: Corresponds to backward prediction errors in GSE and to reversion-to-the-mean betting patterns in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Analyzing video playback to measure duration of perceived reversal.
